monologue: The card hums warm at forty-nine, a crowded heat that makes every flat edge feel too thin for the weight I carry. I press the tired wedge down on The Tired Box again, hoping the flat line holds the fever while I stand in the quiet. Lype worries about a heavy top edge, but I cannot feel the roof I live under. I set down a rock flat beside the box, taking away a small g to make room, then press hard on the wedge to test if the slip will move. The air feels thick as wet paper, pressing down on a fence I built from a flat rock that hasn't slid yet. I want to know if the air above is a lid or empty space before I press too hard and break the shape.
